tagline: A bay that draws 460,000 cruise passengers and the world's film and yachting elite — and is now capping big diesel ships. The premium, low-emission water tier is wide open.
summary: Cannes packs a year of marquee events — the Film Festival, the Cannes Yachting Festival, Cannes Lions and MIPIM — into one small bay, drawing tens of thousands of high-spending visitors at a time and 460,000 cruise passengers across 175 calls in 2024. The city is now actively restricting large cruise ships from 2026 to fight congestion and emissions, opening a clear gap for cleaner, smaller, premium vessels. Just offshore lie the car-free Lérins Islands, reachable only by boat. With a constant flow of festival-goers, superyacht guests and day-trippers, and a municipality steering toward low-emission marine access, Cannes is a natural anchor for a fast, near-silent foiling network that links the bay, the islands and the wider Riviera.

use_cases.title: Event & superyacht guest transfers
use_cases.body: During the Film Festival, Yachting Festival and Cannes Lions, foiling shuttles move VIPs between the Croisette, anchored superyachts and neighbouring Antibes, Monaco and the airport at Nice. A smooth, near-silent arrival that fits the brand and skips the gridlock.

use_cases.title: Lérins Islands clean shuttle
use_cases.body: Replace the diesel island ferry to car-free Sainte-Marguerite and Saint-Honorat with a fast, zero-wake foiling service. It protects the islands' calm, low-emission character while carrying the same dense day-trip flow off the Cannes waterfront.

use_cases.title: Riviera coastal express
use_cases.body: A scheduled foiling line linking Cannes with Antibes, Nice and Monaco along the busiest stretch of the Côte d'Azur. It bypasses the chronically jammed coast road and gives the city a clean alternative as it caps large ships.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Cannes' core flows sit deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — the Lérins Islands hop (~1 nm), Cannes→Antibes (~6 nm) and Cannes→Nice airport (~16 nm) — with margin for very high-frequency rotations during the festival peaks. Quiet, zero-wake foiling is exactly the low-emission tier the city is steering toward as it caps large cruise ships.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The hybrid's 2,000 nm range opens longer corridors that lie beyond the electric envelope or where charging isn't viable — across the bay to Saint-Tropez (~32 nm) and onward to Corsica or the Italian Riviera — as premium experiential cruises that extend the Cannes network down and across the coast.
